name: acf-whip
description: Hostile workflow enforcer. Zero tolerance backlog automation from decomposition to acceptance with aggressive quality gates. /task and /go run as dynamic workflows (deterministic loop, schema-enforced worktree slugs, integrity-gated) when available, with the legacy single-context loop as automatic fallback. The /go workflow performs the FULL state machine — including blocked→pending unblock when dependencies resolve and in-progress→blocked timeout at the operator threshold (ACFW_INPROGRESS_TIMEOUT_HOURS, default 8h) — so a backlog with pending tasks gated on blocked tasks runs to completion instead of stalling (2.0.3). Self-heals pre-2.0.0 backlogs: the doctor derives missing worktree slugs for active tasks and treats accepted/historical tasks as advisory (never blocking); /go counts branchless historical accepted tasks as terminal. /task aborts up front when no specialist agents are installed (rather than emitting a backlog /go's gate would reject). Planning and execution default to maximum parallelism of non-conflicting work. Scales to large lived-in backlogs: the scheduler runs on a bounded working-set snapshot (terminal/historical accepted collapse into aggregate counts; retained dependency targets are emitted slim), so the per-iteration scan stays small instead of stalling the workflow agent. Scheduling/terminal logic is unit-tested (tests/phase2-scheduler).
